Subject: BRL settlement — correspondent bank fees & VAT implications

Dylan,

Quick one on the upcoming BRL settlement for PayPartner (invoice INV-99821): our treasury needs to know how Redwood wants correspondent/intermediary bank fees handled on their side. We see two common flows:

1) Sender cover (OUR) — payer instructs their bank to bear all correspondent and intermediary fees so the beneficiary receives the full gross amount.
2) SHA (shared) / beneficiary-net — intermediary fees are deducted along the chain and beneficiary receives net.

Can you confirm which you want for this invoice? If you elect OUR, please confirm whether you will accept the exchange rate applied by the intermediary (if any) or whether you want PayPartner to pass a net amount in BRL.

Also: Brazilian compliance asks that the payer include Redwood's CNPJ on invoices to avoid additional reconciliation delays on our side. Can you confirm whether your invoice will include a CNPJ and whether Redwood requires VAT/PIS/COFINS phrasing on the invoice?

Bank chain (we typically route via ITAÚ as correspondent): attached is a CSV with our preferred nostro/vostro details and suggested BICs — can you verify?

Attachments: paypartner_brl_nostro_details.csv (stub: account numbers + BICs)

Thanks,
Bruno Silva
Head of Treasury — PayPartner

Hi Bruno — thanks for the details and the CSV. Looping in Laura (payments ops) and Sean (billing) to confirm accounting treatment. A couple of clarifying points from our side first: 

- For hosted customer invoices Redwood typically invoices in USD and accepts settlement in local currency where requested; for this PayPartner invoice is the originating invoice expected to be BRL or USD? Prefer USD invoice + BRL settlement unless customer requires a BRL invoice for local tax purposes.

- For correspondent fees: Redwood prefers sender-cover (OUR) when we can control the gross payout amount — that avoids reconciliation headaches where intermediate fees are unpredictable. If PayPartner's standard is SHA, we can accept but need an explicit fee estimate and the ultimate NET amount before applying credits.

- If you can confirm the exact intermediary BICs and whether the intermediary will apply a conversion (e.g., USD->BRL) mid-chain, we can decide to instruct OUR vs SHA on a case-by-case basis. Please confirm the chain and provide the swift BICs and intermediary fee estimates.

Proposed short options (pick one):
A) Redwood instructs OUR for this settlement (Redwood bears intermediary fees). PayPartner confirms final beneficiary account receives gross BRL amount. Redwood will add a line on our invoice: "CNPJ: 12.345.678/0001-90" and note "No VAT charged — cross-border service" if that matches your reconciliation needs.
B) PayPartner takes SHA/beneficiary-net. PayPartner provides guaranteed net amount to Redwood so we can reconcile. Redwood will invoice USD and accept the resulting BRL net amount.

I attached our standard wire template to speed things up. Once you confirm (A or B) and the intermediary chain, Laura will issue final instructions to treasury.

Attachment: redwood_wire_template_v2.pdf (stub)

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks

Dylan,

Appreciate the quick response. Our standard is SHA (intermediary fees deducted) for most SaaS vendors — it's how our domestic payout rails are configured. That said, for enterprise partners we can accept the OUR instruction on a per-payment basis if Redwood covers the estimated intermediary fees up-front. For this payment we can do either but we need confirmation on the chosen flow before we release the net amount to bookkeeping.

Intermediary chain (typical):
- Sender bank (international USD debit) -> ITAÚ Corresp. (BIC: ITAUBRSP) -> Local clearing -> Beneficiary account at Banco do Brasil (BIC: BRASBRSB)
Estimated intermediary fee range: BRL 15–45 depending on correspondent and reference FX margin.

Tax note: there is no federal VAT equivalent to EU VAT for these service imports; however, local municipalities may apply ISS on invoiceed services. To avoid downstream holds, please include Redwood's CNPJ on the invoice and annotate the service as "international software/service — payer liable for local ISS where applicable". Providing the CNPJ will speed reconciliation significantly.

Attachment: bank_chain_diagram.png (stub)

If you choose OUR, please send the final gross BRL figure you expect to be credited to the beneficiary and we will confirm. If SHA, send invoice USD amount and we'll respond with the expected BRL net after intermediaries so you can check reconciliation.

Best,
Bruno
